content.text: The CPC keyword search is returning empty, so I'll go straight to the known solid-electrolyte CPC groups and cross-check with a keyword-based analytics query.

tool_use_meta.display_name: Technology landscape for a CPC prefix
Technology landscape for a CPC prefix

content.text:
**Toyota leads solid-state battery patenting, with Panasonic and Samsung SDI close behind.** Japan and Korea own the field. Chinese companies file heavily at home but are not yet among the top owners.

I measured this two ways. The first is the CPC class for inorganic solid electrolytes in secondary cells (H01M10/0562), counted by patent family since 2016 from PATSTAT 2026 Spring. The second is a keyword count of publications mentioning solid-state batteries or solid electrolytes since 2016 from a Google Patents slice dated 2026-07-07. Both give the same leaders.

| Rank | Applicant | Families (CPC, since 2016) | Publications (keyword, since 2016) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Toyota | 610 | 3,175 (two name variants combined) |
| 2 | Panasonic | 507 | 2,154 |
| 3 | Samsung SDI | 463 | 1,081 |
| 4 | LG Energy Solution | 313 | 1,202 |
| 5 | Hyundai + Kia | 268 + 376 | 875 + 776 |
| 6 | Samsung Electronics | 267 | 612 |
| 7 | Chinese Academy of Sciences | 230 | not in top 20 |
| 8 | Honda | 197 | 626 |
| 9 | Murata | 165 | 755 |
| 10 | Fujifilm, LG Chem, Idemitsu Kosan | 112 to 130 each | 575 to 587 each |

Some things worth knowing beyond the ranking:

- **Hyundai and Kia together rival Panasonic.** Their families are split across two Kia name clusters plus Hyundai. Combined they are roughly the second-largest filer, and Kia is the fastest-growing new entrant since 2021.
- **Japan dominates on R&D origin.** Japanese applicants hold about 3,900 families in the CPC class, Korea about 2,500, the US about 1,500, and China only about 370. That last figure understates China because many Chinese applicants have no recorded country.
- **China is the biggest filing destination.** About 8,200 families are filed in China versus 6,100 in the US. Chinese firms like Geely, Svolt, and CATL are the main new entrants, but none yet reach the top ten by ownership.
- **Materials suppliers are a distinct tier.** Idemitsu Kosan, Mitsui Mining & Smelting, NGK Insulators, TDK, and Fujifilm hold large positions in sulfide and oxide electrolyte materials rather than cells.
- **Growth is steep.** Families in the CPC class grew from about 460 in 2016 to about 1,800 in 2023. The 2024 and 2025 figures look lower only because of publication lag.
- **US startups are seminal but small.** The most-cited families come from PolyPlus, QuantumScape, and Sakti3-era work on protected lithium anodes and garnet electrolytes. They matter for licensing and litigation more than for volume.

One caveat: the broader electrolyte-materials class (H01M10/056) puts LG Energy Solution and CATL on top, but that class also covers liquid and gel electrolytes, so it is not a solid-state measure. Applicant names are harmonized clusters, so small counts for the same company may be split across variants.
